There will be minor CO 2 losses throughout the process. Some CO 2 losses to atmosphere that may take place in the facility include: the dehydration unit flash gas and regeneration streams that will be vented to the atmosphere and the CO 2 dissolved in the water that is removed in the compressor inter-stages; however, the quantity of CO 2 in these areas should be low. Process Control and Monitoring Requirements The CO 2 processing and injection facility will be controlled by the existing control system in the OEE facility and monitored by operations staff around the clock. It is likely that a custody transfer quality flow meter will be required on the injection outlet of the facility. Other instrumentation will be standard pressure, temperature, and flow instruments. There is no need to control the flow, temperature, or pressure of the compressed and dehydrated CO 2 to specifications outside of the values listed in Table 5. In other words, flow or pressure tests at certain conditions will not be required and the facility will just compress and dehydrate the CO 2 available from the fermenters during normal operations. Reliability and Operability Requirements Major rotating equipment will not be spared as part of this project. Minor higher-maintenance equipment like cooling water pumps and filters that are regularly changed out will be spared.
